prompt:
You are writing the transition rule of an unknown grid game.
The board is a list of 64 strings of 64 characters, one character per cell.
The action is 'DOWN'. When the action is a tuple, the numbers are a row and a column.
Below are recent transitions caused by this action. Only the cells that changed are
listed as (row, col): old->new; every other cell stayed the same.

example 1: nothing changed
example 2: (63,60): c->B
example 3: (63,59): c->B
example 4: (21,24): g->B, (22,23): g->B, (22,24): g->B, (22,25): g->B, (23,22): g->B, (23,23): g->B, (23,24): p->B, (23,25): g->B, (23,26): g->B, (24,21): g->B, (24,22): g->B, (24,23): p->B, (24,24): p->B, (24,25): p->B, (24,26): g->B, (24,27): g->B, (25,20): g->B, (25,21): g->B, (25,22): p->B, (25,23): p->B, (25,24): p->B, (25,25): p->B, (25,26): p->B, (25,27): g->B, (25,28): g->B, (26,19): g->B, (26,20): g->B, (26,21): p->B, (26,22): p->B, (26,23): p->B, (26,24): p->B, (26,25): p->B, (26,26): p->B, (26,27): p->B, (26,28): g->B, (26,29): g->B, (27,18): g->B, (27,19): g->B, (27,20): p->B, (27,21): p->B, (27,22): p->B, (27,23): p->B, (27,24): p->B, (27,25): p->B, (27,26): p->B, (27,27): p->B, (27,28): p->B, (27,29): g->B ...

Write one Python function `def predict(board, action)` that returns the next board
as a list of strings and reproduces every example above exactly. Prefer a rule that
depends on what is on the board (find things by their character and move or recolour
them) over fixed coordinates, so the rule keeps working when things have moved.
Return only the code, no explanation, no markdown fences.
response:
```python
def predict(board, action):
    if isinstance(action, tuple):
        row, col = action
    else:
        row, col = action[0], action[1]

    if row < 0 or row > 63 or col < 0 or col > 63:
        return board

    old_char = board[row][col]
    new_char = 'B' if old_char == 'g' else old_char

    # Create a copy of the board
    next_board = [row[:] for row in board]

    # Move the character down
    next_board[row][col] = new_char

    # Update the cells below
    for i in range(row+1, 64):
        next_board[i][col] = 'B' if next_board[i-1][col] == 'g' else next_board[i-1][col]

    return next_board
```
